body:
Security review of the server API (2026-09-19), finding 2 of 4.

`audit.record` joins `key=value` with spaces and writes `str(value)` verbatim. Two values are client-controlled: `platform` on `auth.login` (any JSON value, up to the 4 MB body cap) and `path` on `authz.denied` and `db.contention` (`request.path` is percent-decoded, so `%0A` is a newline). Confirmed: logging in with `"platform": "web\nevent=admin.user_deleted outcome=ok"` writes a second, forged audit line; an unauthenticated request to a dynamic route such as `/api/v1/lists/x%0Aevent=.../members` does the same through the 401 path. Anyone reading the audit log for incidents can be misled, and a long value bloats it.

Fix in `audit.record`, not at the call sites: render every value through one sanitizer — control characters (at least `\r`, `\n`, `\t`) escaped or replaced, length capped (200 characters is plenty for an id, a path or a platform), non-strings via `repr`. Test with the two vectors above.
title: Audit log: escape control characters and cap client-controlled values
